messages:
maria: Heads-up — during the v2 kernel rollout load test I saw a ~12-18% bump in p99 on host ingress. Flamegraphs point at tokenization + request header parsing as the hot path.

Tom: Any pprof or trace snippets? Is this HTTP/2 or gRPC path?

maria: Both, but gRPC hot a bit worse. Quick pprof top: 
```
34.8%  Tokenizer::tokenize_loop
18.3%  grpc::serializer::parse_headers
12.1%  host::preparse::frame_coalesce
6.5%   syscalls::writev
```
Numbers from canary cluster under 500 rps/client burst.

sasha: Did anything change in the kernel picker lately? More fallbacks to compat kernels for short sequences could reduce batching density and increase host overhead.

maria: Yes — kernel-picker 3.1 lowered the sequence-length affinity threshold to prefer small-seq optimized kernels. Outcome: average batch-size down from 8.6 -> 5.1 on these workloads. That reduces GPU efficiency but also seems to blow up host preparse costs (more per-request work).

Tom: That matches the writev signature — more small writes per request. Also if we shorten the autobatch window we might see more small batches. What are current batching heuristics?

maria: Autobatch window = 5ms (prod canary nodes). Kernel affinity: threshold_seq = 64 -> changed to 32. KV cache warmup shows more misses too. kvcache_hit_rate went 0.92 -> 0.85.

sasha: So two amplifiers: smaller minibatches (host does work per request more often) + worse KV hits (more model work + cache fetch overhead). Hypothesis: host CPU dominated by tokenization & header parsing because per-request overhead now amortized less.

Tom: Quick mitigation experiments? Can we temporarily revert affinity threshold and bump autobatch window to 12ms on a subset?

maria: I ran an A/B yesterday: 50% nodes reverted -> results: p99 dropped ~6% relative to canary w/3.1, p50 unchanged. Increasing autobatch to 12ms gave additional ~4% p99 improvement but increased median CPU on proxy by ~8% (more memcopy/hold). Raw numbers:
```
canary(3.1, 5ms): p99=220ms, p50=28ms, cpu_proxy=62%
revert-affinity:  p99=207ms, p50=27ms, cpu_proxy=63%
revert+12ms:      p99=199ms, p50=28ms, cpu_proxy=71%
```
So batching window helps latency tail but increases host CPU and memory pressure.

sasha: What about tokenization micro-optimizations? We saw a decent win in the past from vectorized UTF8 scanning and reusing a per-thread tokenizer buffer (vs per-request alloc).

maria: I prototyped reusing tokenizer_buffers (size 8k) and a coalesced header parser that reads consecutive small gRPC header frames into one parse op. Quick local bench: tokenization cpu down 18% on microbench, and syscalls/writev reduced by 40% in the smallwrite case.

Tom: Nice. Can you paste the coalesce snippet (pseudo)? We might ship as a hotfix to canary service.

maria: Sure — pseudo: 
```
// coalesce consecutive small header frames (<=256B) into single parse
while (frames_in_buf && frames.peek().size <= 256) {
  coalesced.append(frames.pop().payload);
  if (coalesced.size >= 1500) break; // avoid giant copy
}
parse_headers(coalesced);
```
This reduces per-frame parse calls and lowers syscall churn.

sasha: Also look at kvcache policy — eviction churn rose. Might be due to smaller batch shapes causing different KV footprint. If we raise per-shard cache TTL or tweak LRU window we can recover hit rate without changing kernels.

maria: Good call. I ran a TTL bump + slightly larger shard size for A nodes: kvcache_hit_rate recovered to 0.90 and p99 improved ~3% vs revert-affinity baseline.

Tom: So combined plan: 
- revert affinity change in kernel-picker (short term)
- enable tokenizer_buffer reuse and header coalescing (hotfix on canary)
- adjust kvcache shard sizing/TTL (config change)
- keep autobatch window at 5ms for now, but monitor throughput/latency tradeoffs

sasha: Sounds good. Can we add a perf regression test that simulates many small requests (median tokens 6, payload 200B) and measures kvcache_hit + writev rate + kernel selection distribution? Want guardrails before any future kernel-picker change.

maria: I'll add a replay test in perf-suite and a tracing assert for writev/rpc-smallwrite ratio. Also will roll the tokenizer hotfix to 10% canary after unit tests.

deploy-bot: Deploy (canary) scheduled: tokenizer-buffer-reuse v1.0 -> 10% at 5678904380 :rocket:

Tom: Thanks. One more ask — add a simple flamegraph snapshot step to the rollout checklist so we catch host-preparse regressions earlier.

maria: Will do, adding checklist item + perf-suite job. Action items: maria (hotfix + perf tests), sasha (kvcache config), tom (add flamegraph step to rollout doc).

maria: tagging @sasha @tom for visibility :eyes:
